The DeepSeek API uses an API format compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic. By modifying the configuration, you can use the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK or softwares compatible with the OpenAI/Anthropic API to access the DeepSeek API.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is now available on the DeepSeek API with native multimodal support.

If you need higher concurrency, you can submit a capacity expansion request. We will match the appropriate concurrency based on your actual business needs. There is no additional cost for capacity expansion.
Model was released and it's amazing. Frontier level (better than Opus 4.6) at a fraction of the cost.
The Flash version is 284B A13B in mixed FP8/FP4 and native precision weights total ~154 GB, KV cache 10% as much as V3 - very accessible for people running large local models.
I like the pelican I got out of deepseek-v4-flash more than the one I got from deepseek-v4-pro (comparing outputs across DeepSeek 3.1, 3.2, and v4 via OpenRouter).
Excited that the long awaited v4 is finally out. But feel sad that it's not multimodal native.
Initial impressions: this is a really strong model and the fact that they reduced prices at the same time makes it an awesome backup model to use when your primary subscription runs out.
It also seems to be more willing to just do whatever you ask of it... US models (except Grok) have a tendency to refuse [downloading a ROM I legally own], Chinese models happily oblige.
A very powerful model, and with multimodal support now, it can be used as a primary model.
I highly doubt that it goes past Kimi K3 in actual practice. GLM 5.3 claimed the same, but in practice, K3 is so damn knowledgeable, I suspect due to its massive size.
Holy moly.. even just the Llama 8B model trained on R1 outputs (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B), according to these benchmarks, is stronger than Claude 3.5 Sonnet (except on GPQA).
I've been using it. Completely overhyped trash. Does well in benchmarks and fails in real-world scenarios.

I was initially enthusiastic about DS3, because of the price, but eventually I learned: function calling is broken (excessive duplicated FC, hallucinated names/params); response quality is poor for code generation; support is not responding.
These models always seem great, until you actually use them for real tasks. The reliability goes way down, you can't trust the output like you can with even a lower end model like 4o.
Amazing progress with this budget. My only concern is that on openrouter.ai it says this provider may use your prompts and completions to train new models - this is a dealbreaker for me.

For months now I've seen benchmarks for lots of models that beat Claude 3.5 Sonnet, but when I actually try to use those models (using Cline VSCode plugin) they never work as well as Claude for programming.

I tried the same tests on DeepSeek-R1 just now, and it did much better [than earlier DeepThink]. While still not as good as o1, its answers no longer contained obviously misguided analyses or hallucinated solutions.
It already replaces o1 Pro in many cases for me today. It's much faster than o1 Pro and results are good in most cases... Also a lot more fun reading the reasoning chatter.

One point is reliability, as others have mentioned. Another important point for me is censorship. Due to their political nature, the model seemed to be heavily censored on topics such as the CCP and Taiwan.
Great, I've found DeepSeek to consistently be a better programmer than Chat GPT or Claude.
Amazing progress by open-source. However, the 64K input tokens and especially the 8K output token limit can be frustrating vs o1's 200K/100K limit. Still, at 1/30th the API cost this is huge.

Deepseek is well known to have ripped off OpenAI APIs extensively in post training, embarrassingly so that it sometimes calls itself 'As a model made by OpenAI'. At least don't use the hosted version unless you want your data to go to China.

Model lifecycle handled via dated notices in the News/updates changelog: "The two legacy API model names, `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner`, will be discontinued in three months (2026-07-24). During the current period, these two model names point to the non-thinking mode and thinking mode" of the current model — advance notice with alias mapping.
Streaming documented in the first-call guide: "This is a non-stream example, you can set the `stream` parameter to `true` to get stream response", in both OpenAI and Anthropic API formats.

A dedicated "Rate Limit & Isolation" page documents concurrency limits (pricing page tables show per-model concurrency, e.g. 2500/500) and the keep-alive behavior under load ("Streaming requests: Continuously return SSE keep-alive comments"); the error-codes page documents 429 semantics.
A maintained function-calling guide with runnable OpenAI-format examples (stream or non-stream) — tool use is a documented first-class capability of the API.
